title: Mini Blueberry Olive Oil Cake (Gluten Free & Dairy Free)
description: This mini blueberry olive oil cake is gluten free, dairy free, and refined sugar free. Made in one bowl with wholesome ingredients, it's soft, fluffy, and bursting with juicy blueberries.

hero.alt: A hand holding a slice of mini blueberry olive oil loaf cake showing the golden crumb with jammy blueberries throughout

thumbnail.alt: A hand holding a slice of mini blueberry olive oil loaf cake showing the golden crumb with juicy blueberries

instructions.text: In a bowl add the 2 eggs, olive oil, almond butter, maple syrup and vanilla extract. Whisk together until combined.
Fold in the coconut sugar, oat flour, almond flour and baking powder until just combined. Do not overmix.
Transfer the batter to a small lined loaf tin.
Bake for 40–45 minutes or until a skewer inserted in the centre comes out clean.
Allow to cool fully before slicing and enjoying.

notes: Do not overmix the batter to keep the cake fluffy.
If using frozen blueberries, fold them in gently to prevent colour bleeding.
Let the loaf cool fully before slicing to prevent crumbling.
Store in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days or in the refrigerator for up to 5 days.

story.subtitle: gluten free, dairy free & refined sugar free
paragraphs: if you love a soft, fluffy loaf cake but want something a little lighter and made with more wholesome ingredients, this mini blueberry olive oil cake is exactly that. it's small enough that it doesn't turn into a five day leftover situation, but it still has that proper loaf cake feel when you cut into it, which is honestly the balance i'm always going for with these recipes.

it's gluten free, dairy free and refined sugar free, and the whole thing comes together in one bowl, which is one of my favourite things about it. there's no creaming butter and sugar, no separate bowls for wet and dry, you just whisk the eggs, olive oil, almond butter, maple syrup and vanilla together, fold in the dry ingredients, then fold in the blueberries and pour it straight into the tin. less washing up, and honestly, less washing up is often the difference between actually making something on a tuesday night and just thinking about it.

fresh blueberries are what i use, and i'd stick with them if you can get good ones, since they hold their shape a little better in the batter. if all you've got is frozen though, they'll work just as well, you just want to skip thawing them first because that extra moisture can throw the batter off. either way, tossing them in a teaspoon of oat flour before you fold them in helps stop them all sinking straight to the bottom, which is such a small step but makes a real difference. blueberries are also one of the more antioxidant dense fruits you can bake with, the anthocyanins that give them that deep blue purple colour are the same compounds behind a lot of their health reputation.

the olive oil stands in for butter here, keeping the crumb moist and tender, and it means the ingredient list stays short and the whole loaf stays dairy free without any awkward substituting. it's got such a mild, slightly fruity flavour that you honestly wouldn't clock it's in there once the cake is baked, and it keeps things moist for longer than butter tends to, which is a nice bonus if you're not planning on finishing the whole loaf in one sitting. there's a nutritional upside too, olive oil is rich in polyphenols and monounsaturated fats, both linked to lower inflammation and better heart health, so it's a swap that pays off beyond just flavour.

the almond butter earns its place here too, it's what actually binds the batter together alongside the eggs, so it's not just an add on for flavour. it brings healthy fats and protein along with it, and that combination helps slow down how quickly the maple syrup and coconut sugar hit your blood sugar, so you get a steadier lift rather than a spike.

almond flour and oat flour are what give the loaf its structure while keeping everything gluten free, and they do really different jobs here. the almond flour brings healthy fats and a slightly nutty richness, while the oat flour is what gives you that light, soft crumb you'd expect from a normal loaf cake. together they hold up properly when you slice into it, which isn't always something you can say about gluten free bakes.

you can swap the blueberries out for raspberries, blackberries or diced strawberries if you want to switch things up, the method stays exactly the same either way. if i'm honest though, a teaspoon of fresh lemon zest stirred in with the wet ingredients is one of my favourite additions here, it brightens the whole loaf without needing any actual lemon juice. blueberry, olive oil and lemon might be one of my favourite flavour combinations in baking, full stop.
if you love fruit forward bakes, try my sugar free apple fritters or my sugar free blueberry fritters next.

this batter also works really well as muffins if that's more useful to you. just divide it between a lined muffin tin and cut the bake time down to 18 to 22 minutes, or until a skewer comes out clean, they're honestly great for meal prep or lunchboxes if a whole loaf is more cake than you actually need in one go!

let the loaf cool completely before you slice it, i know it's tempting not to but it's what stops it crumbling apart instead of cutting cleanly. after that it keeps well, an airtight container at room temperature for a couple of days, up to five in the fridge, or wrap individual slices and freeze them for up to a month if you want one on standby.

faq.question: How do I store this mini blueberry olive oil cake?
faq.answer: Store the loaf in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days or in the refrigerator for up to 5 days. Allow it to come to room temperature before serving for the best texture. You can also freeze individual slices wrapped in cling film for up to 1 month, simply thaw at room temperature for about 30 minutes before eating.

faq.question: Can I use frozen blueberries in a blueberry loaf cake?
faq.answer: Yes, you can use frozen blueberries in this mini blueberry olive oil cake. Do not thaw them before adding to the batter, as this can release excess moisture and affect the texture. Tossing them lightly in oat flour before folding into the batter can help prevent sinking and reduce colour bleeding into the crumb.

faq.question: Is this mini blueberry olive oil cake gluten free?
faq.answer: Yes, this blueberry olive oil loaf cake is completely gluten free as long as you use certified gluten free ingredients. The recipe uses almond flour and oat flour, both naturally gluten free. If you are highly sensitive, look for certified gluten free oat flour as oats can sometimes be cross-contaminated in processing.

faq.question: Is this blueberry olive oil cake dairy free?
faq.answer: Yes, this recipe is naturally dairy free since it uses olive oil instead of butter. There are no dairy ingredients in this recipe at all, making it suitable for dairy-free and lactose-intolerant diets.

faq.question: Why use olive oil in cake?
faq.answer: Olive oil helps create a moist, tender crumb while adding subtle richness. It also keeps the cake soft for longer compared to butter-based cakes and makes the recipe dairy free! The flavour of olive oil in baking is mild and slightly fruity, which pairs beautifully with the blueberries without being at all overpowering.

faq.question: Why did my blueberries sink to the bottom?
faq.answer: Blueberries can sink if the batter is too thin or if the berries are very large and heavy. To help prevent sinking, toss the blueberries lightly in a teaspoon of oat flour before folding them into the batter. The flour coating helps them stay suspended. Also, make sure you fold them in gently rather than stirring vigorously. The batter for this recipe is thicker than many standard loaf cakes, which naturally helps keep the berries in place.

faq.question: Can I substitute almond butter in this blueberry olive oil cake?
faq.answer: Yes. Cashew butter is the closest substitute and gives a very similar neutral, creamy flavour. Sunflower seed butter also works well if you need a nut-free option, though it may give a slightly more earthy taste. Tahini can work too but will give the cake a more distinctive, sesame-forward flavour that not everyone loves in a sweet bake.

faq.question: Can I make this cake without coconut sugar?
faq.answer: Yes. Brown sugar or muscovado sugar are the most easy direct substitutes, though they are refined sugars. For a refined sugar-free alternative, you can increase the maple syrup by an extra tablespoon and reduce the liquid in the recipe slightly to compensate. Monkfruit sweetener also works well as a 1:1 swap for coconut sugar.

faq.question: Can I make this blueberry olive oil cake as muffins?
faq.answer: Yes, this batter translates really well into muffins! Divide the batter evenly between a lined or greased muffin tin and reduce the baking time to around 18 to 22 minutes, or until a skewer inserted in the centre comes out clean. The muffins will be slightly smaller than a loaf slice but just as moist and fluffy. They're great for meal prep or on-the-go snacking.

faq.question: Can I add lemon to this blueberry olive oil cake?
faq.answer: Yes, and it's a really lovely addition! Stir a teaspoon of fresh lemon zest into the batter along with the other wet ingredients for a subtle citrus note that brightens up the blueberry flavour beautifully. You can also add a teaspoon of fresh lemon juice for a slightly more pronounced tang. The combination of blueberry, olive oil, and lemon is one of my favourite flavour pairings in baking.

tips: Do not overmix the batter to keep the cake fluffy.
If using frozen blueberries, fold them in gently to prevent colour bleeding.
Let the loaf cool fully before slicing to prevent crumbling.
Toss the blueberries in a teaspoon of oat flour before folding them into the batter — this helps stop them sinking to the bottom during baking.
